sections.heading: Typography Matters
sections.text: Good typography is invisible. Bad typography is everywhere. The Inter typeface family was designed for computer screens and features a tall x-height to aid in readability of mixed-case and lower-case text.

sections.heading: Font Weights
sections.text: Inter comes in multiple weights from Thin (100) to Black (900). In this test we use Regular (400) and Bold (700) to demonstrate that both weights are correctly loaded and rendered in the PDF.

sections.heading: Pagination Accuracy
sections.text: Custom fonts have different metrics than system fonts. If the font is not loaded during measurement, text will be measured with the wrong font, leading to incorrect page breaks. sections.heading: International Characters
sections.text: Inter has excellent support for international characters: French (e, a, u, c), German (u, o, a, ss), Spanish (n, i), and many more. The font file we're using contains the full Latin character set.

sections.heading: Numbers and Symbols
sections.text: Tabular figures are important for invoices and financial documents: 1,234,567.89 EUR. Inter provides well-designed numerals that align vertically in tables, making columns of numbers easy to read.

sections.heading: Code and Technical Content
sections.text: While Inter is a sans-serif typeface, it works well alongside monospace fonts for technical documentation. The clear letterforms help distinguish similar characters like 0/O, 1/l/I, and rn/m.
